mainTopic: Refuting רבי אלעזר and שמואל, why a missing guarantee counts as a scribe's mistake in loans but not in sales, and אביי's rulings on sellers in court
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of a ברייתא that refutes רבי אלעזר. The גמרא explains that his two refuted points are really one, and then shows that the same ברייתא refutes שמואל on two points. One of those points is his rule that a found שטר הקנאה is returned with no worry about פרעון. Next, שמואל explains that the חכמים treat a missing אחריות clause as a טעות סופר. That seems to clash with another rule of his: a scribe must ask before writing guarantee terms in a sale. The גמרא resolves this by splitting loans from sales. Nobody lends money without security, but a buyer may knowingly buy land with no guarantee. A real case of אבוה בר איהי, who bought a room from his sister, shows שמואל ruling this way. The amud ends with rulings of אביי about when a seller may argue in court against his creditor, and it begins a new case about challengers to a field that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Both of רבי אלעזר's points come from one reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the two refuted points of רבי אלעזר are really one, because his explanation of רבי מאיר follows from where he places the dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is really one thing, because it is one reason. Since רבי אלעזר says the dispute is in a case where the borrower does not admit, that is why he explains רבי מאיר this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question: why say the ברייתא refutes רבי אלעזר on 'two' points? The answer is that both points really count as one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר placed the dispute in a case where the borrower does not admit. Because of that, he had to explain רבי מאיר as holding that a note without אחריות cannot collect even from free property. The second point grows out of the first, so it is one mistake, not two.

keyTerms.meaning: It is one (one point, not two)
one reason
the one who owes (the borrower) admits
explains, works out the meaning

phrases.english: It is one,
for it is one reason;
because Rabbi Elazar says
the dispute is where the liable party does not admit,
he explains it this way.
phrases.notes: He means רבי אלעזר explains רבי מאיר's view this way: a note without a property guarantee can't collect even from unsold property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from before this section about why the refutation of רבי אלעזר was counted as two points.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Merging: the two points share one underlying reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like רבי אלעזר made two separate mistakes.
steps.terutzMaskana: His explanation of רבי מאיר follows from where he places the dispute, so it counts as one point.

steps.title: שמואל is refuted, first point: same as רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא also refutes שמואל on two points. The first is that he, like רבי אלעזר, sets the משנה in a case where the borrower does not admit.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a refutation of שמואל on two points. One is like רבי אלעזר, because שמואל also sets our משנה in a case where the borrower does not admit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the same ברייתא against שמואל and says it refutes him on two points. This step gives the first point and sets up the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל read the משנה the same way as רבי אלעזר: the dispute is when the borrower does not admit. The ברייתא shows there is no dispute in that case, so שמואל falls together with רבי אלעזר here.

keyTerms.meaning: a conclusive refutation
in two things, on two points
sets up the case as, explains as referring to

phrases.english: A refutation of Shmuel on two points:
one is like Rabbi Elazar,
for he sets up our mishna
in a case where the liable party does not admit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same ברייתא to a second אמורא, שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading that the משנה's dispute is where the borrower does not admit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows there is no dispute in that case, so placing the dispute there is wrong.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: a found deed of transfer is returned
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a שטר הקנאה found in the market is returned to its owner, and we do not worry that the debt was already paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second point is what שמואל said: if someone found a שטר הקנאה in the market, he should return it to the owner, and we are not concerned that it was already paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes שמואל's rule about a found document. This sets up the second refutation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a found loan document raises the fear of פרעון. The debt may have been paid, and the creditor might use the document again unfairly. שמואל says that for a שטר הקנאה we do not worry about this, so the finder returns it.

keyTerms.meaning: a deed of transfer, where the borrower gives the lender rights to his property
repayment (the worry that the debt was already paid)
we are not concerned

phrases.english: And the other is what Shmuel said:
If one found a deed of transfer in the marketplace,
he must return it to the owner,
and we are not concerned about repayment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the second of the two points on which שמואל is refuted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A found שטר הקנאה is returned to its owner; we do not suspect פרעון.

steps.title: The ברייתא shows we do worry about repayment
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a found document is not returned even when both sides admit, so we do worry about פרעון. This worry is even stronger in שמואל's case, where the borrower does not admit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation, since the ברייתא teaches that even if both admit, the finder returns it to neither one. So we are concerned about repayment. Even more so here, where the borrower does not admit, we are concerned about repayment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to knock down שמואל's rule about the found שטר הקנאה. It uses a קל וחומר: if we worry when both admit, we surely worry when the borrower does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, both lender and borrower say the debt is still owed, and still the document is not returned. That can only be because of a fear of פרעון. In שמואל's case the borrower is not admitting anything, so that fear is stronger, and שמואל's ruling stands refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: even though both of them admit
apparently, this shows
all the more so
the borrower

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא refutes שמואל twice. First, the משנה's dispute is not about a case where the borrower does not admit. Second, we do worry about פרעון with a found document, even more so when the borrower does not admit.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'all the more so' runs from the easier case to the harder one. If we worry about repayment even when the borrower agrees he still owes, we surely worry when he does not agree.

phrases.english: It is refuted, for it teaches here:
even though both of them admit,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַחְזִיר לֹא לָזֶה וְלֹא לָזֶה,
phrases.english: he should not return it, neither to this one nor to that one.
Apparently we are concerned about repayment.
And all the more so here,
phrases.notes: Now 'here' means שמואל's case of the found deed of transfer.

phrases.english: where the borrower does not admit,
we are concerned about repayment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's rule quoted in step 3 using the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that we do not worry about פרעון for a found שטר הקנאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: the ברייתא worries about פרעון even when both sides admit, so we must surely worry when the borrower does not admit.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's rule is refuted; we do suspect פרעון with a found document.

steps.title: שמואל explains the רבנן's reasoning: a missing guarantee is a scribe's mistake
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the חכמים hold that if a loan document has no אחריות clause, the scribe simply left it out by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: What is the reason of the חכמים? They hold that leaving out the guarantee clause is a scribe's mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from שמואל that explains why the חכמים let a lender collect from sold property even when the document has no guarantee clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the חכמים, the guarantee is assumed to be part of every loan. If the document leaves it out, we treat that as the scribe's error, not as a real agreement without a guarantee. That is why the lender can still collect from property the borrower later sold.

keyTerms.meaning: A property guarantee: the borrower's land is pledged as security, so the lender can collect even from land the borrower later sold
A scribe's mistake: something left out or written wrongly by the writer of the document
The חכמים, the majority Sages who disagree with רבי מאיר

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
What is the reason of the Rabbis?
They hold that the guarantee is a scribe's mistake.
phrases.notes: He means that leaving the guarantee out of the document was the scribe's mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the refutation of שמואל to a new statement of his that explains the חכמים' view on guarantee clauses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, a loan document missing the אחריות clause is read as if the clause were there, because leaving it out was a טעות סופר.

steps.title: Another statement of שמואל seems to contradict him
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר איתי cites שמואל's rule that a scribe must ask the seller about writing improvement, best-land and lien terms. That suggests a guarantee is not automatic.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר איתי said to רב אידי בר אבין: Did שמואל really say this? But שמואל said that for improvement value, best-quality land and a lien, the scribe must ask first!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר איתי challenges the previous statement by pointing to a different ruling of שמואל that seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a guarantee is so obvious that leaving it out counts as a mistake, the scribe should just write it in. But שמואל elsewhere says the scribe must ask before writing guarantee terms like שעבוד. That implies a guarantee is not taken for granted.

keyTerms.meaning: Improvement: the added value the buyer built into the field, which the seller must repay if the field is taken away
Best-quality: payment for the loss is taken from the seller's best land
A lien: the seller pledges his properties as security
Must consult: the scribe has to ask the party before writing this term

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר אִיתַּי לְרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: Rava bar Ittai said to Rav Idi bar Avin:
And did Shmuel really say this?
But didn't Shmuel say:
Improvement, best-quality land, and a lien require consulting!
phrases.notes: Before writing these guarantee terms into a sale document, the scribe has to ask the seller whether he agrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the statement in step 5 using a contradicting statement from the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that a missing אחריות clause is a טעות סופר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a guarantee is assumed automatically, a scribe would not need to ask before writing it. Yet שמואל requires asking, so he seems to hold that guarantees are not automatic.

steps.title: Did different people report שמואל differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that perhaps the two statements come from two people who disagreed about what שמואל held.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that whoever reported this statement did not report that one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way out: maybe two different students reported שמואל's view, and each reported only one of the statements. This sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two reporters disagreed, there would be no contradiction inside שמואל's own words, just a dispute about what he said. The גמרא raises this but would prefer a solution in which both statements are true.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say: introduces a suggestion the גמרא usually ends up rejecting

keyTerms.term: מַאן דְּאָמַר הָא לָא אָמַר הָא
keyTerms.meaning: The one who said this did not say that: the two statements come from different reporters

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא מַאן דְּאָמַר הָא לָא אָמַר הָא?
phrases.english: Shall we say that the one who said this did not say that?
phrases.notes: He means the two statements in שמואל's name were reported by different people who disagreed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מַאן דְּאָמַר הָא לָא אָמַר הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the contradiction in step 6 by suggesting a dispute between the people who reported שמואל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the contradiction must be explained as a disagreement between two reporters of שמואל's teaching.

steps.title: Loans and sales are different cases
steps.stepSummary: Both statements are true. In a loan, no one lends without security, so a missing guarantee is a mistake. In a sale, a buyer may take land without a guarantee, so the scribe must ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, it is a loan document, since a person does not give out money for nothing. There, it is buying and selling, since a person may buy land even just for a day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by showing that the two statements of שמואל deal with two different kinds of documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lender always wants security for his money, so a loan document without a guarantee must have a scribe's error. A buyer of land may agree to take the risk without a guarantee, because even owning it for a short time can be worth it. So in a sale, the scribe cannot assume a guarantee and must ask.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan document
Buying and selling: a sale
For nothing, without security
For a day: for a short time only

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל assumes a guarantee in a loan document, because lenders always want security. He does not assume one in a sale document, because a buyer may take the risk, so the scribe must ask.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, it is about a loan document,
phrases.notes: This is the statement in step 5, that a missing guarantee is a scribe's mistake.

phrases.english: since a person does not give money for nothing.
There, it is about buying and selling,
phrases.notes: This is the statement in step 6, that the scribe must ask the seller.

phrases.english: since a person is apt to buy land for a day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea of a dispute between reporters from step 7 and resolves the contradiction from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: each statement of שמואל applies to a different type of document (loan versus sale).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's two statements contradict each other, or they come from reporters who disagreed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A guarantee is assumed in loans, because nobody lends without security, but not in sales, where a buyer may accept the risk. Both statements belong to שמואל and fit together.

steps.title: The story of the room bought from a sister
steps.stepSummary: אבוה בר איהי bought a room from his sister, and her creditor took it from him. שמואל asked whether the sale document had a guarantee. When he said no, שמואל told him there was nothing to collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the case of אבוה בר איהי, who bought an upper room from his sister. Her creditor came and took it from him. He came before מר שמואל. שמואל asked: Did she write you a guarantee? He said: No. שמואל said: If so, go in peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case to show the rule from step 8 in action. In a sale with no written guarantee, שמואל did not assume the guarantee was left out by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said that in a sale a buyer may really agree to buy without a guarantee. Here שמואל rules that way in an actual case: no written guarantee means the buyer cannot go back to the seller. That is why he sends the buyer away empty-handed.

keyTerms.meaning: An upper room or loft
He seized it (a creditor taking property that was owed to him)
A guarantee: the seller promises to pay back if the property is taken away
Go in peace, meaning there is nothing to be done for you here

phrases.english: Like that case of Avuh bar Ihi
who bought an upper room from his sister.
A creditor came and seized it from him.
phrases.notes: This is the sister's creditor. She owed him money, so he had a claim on her property.

phrases.english: He came before Mar Shmuel.
He said to him: Did she write you a guarantee?
He said to him: No.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם כֵּן, זִיל לִשְׁלָמָא.
phrases.english: He said to him: If so, go in peace.
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying: you have no case against your sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the loan-versus-sale split of step 8 in a real ruling of שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: That in a sale, a missing guarantee is not treated as a scribe's mistake.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of אבוה בר איהי, where שמואל ruled that the buyer could not collect from the seller.

steps.title: The buyer reminds שמואל of his own rule
steps.stepSummary: אבוה בר איהי challenges שמואל: didn't you yourself say that a missing guarantee is just a scribe's mistake?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But isn't it the master himself who said that a missing guarantee is a scribe's mistake!
steps.whatsHappening: The buyer pushes back against שמואל, using שמואל's own rule from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 שמואל said that a missing guarantee is just a scribe's mistake. If that applied here, the buyer would have a guarantee and could collect from his sister. So the ruling seems to clash with שמואל's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: A scribe's mistake, something left out of a document by accident
But isn't it you, master, who said

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא מָר הוּא דְּאָמַר
phrases.english: He said to him: But isn't it the master who said
that a missing guarantee is a scribe's mistake!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling in step 9 using his own rule from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the buyer has no guarantee
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל himself said a missing guarantee is a scribe's mistake, so the buyer should be treated as if he had one.

steps.title: שמואל explains: loans yes, sales no
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that his rule applies only to loan documents. In a sale, a person may knowingly buy land with no guarantee, even if it could soon be taken away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That applies to loan documents. But in documents of buying and selling, it does not, because a person does buy land even just for a day.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the buyer's challenge with the same split the גמרא gave in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one lends money without security, so in a loan a missing guarantee must be an accident. But a buyer may knowingly take a risky field, even if he only gets to keep it for a short time. So in a sale, no written guarantee means there really is no guarantee.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to (this case)
Loan documents
Documents of buying and selling
For a day, meaning for a short time

steps.whatToRemember: A missing guarantee is a scribe's mistake in a loan document, but not in a sale document, because a buyer may choose to buy land with no guarantee.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּשְׁטָרֵי הַלְוָאָה,
phrases.english: He said to him: These words apply to loan documents,
but in documents of buying and selling, they do not,
because a person does buy land for a day.
phrases.notes: He means a buyer may take a risky field happily, even if he only gets to use it for a short while.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by limiting the rule to loans.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (loan document versus sale document)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's scribe's-mistake rule seemed to cover every document, sales included.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only loans. In sales, no written guarantee means no guarantee.

steps.title: A seller who gave a guarantee can argue against his creditor
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that if ראובן sold a field to שמעון with a guarantee, and ראובן's creditor comes to take it from שמעון, ראובן may argue the case in court. The creditor cannot push him aside, since the loss will end up falling on ראובן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: ראובן sold a field to שמעון with a guarantee. Then ראובן's creditor came and is taking the field from שמעון. The law is that ראובן may go and argue the case with the creditor. The creditor cannot say to him, 'You are not my opponent in this case,' because ראובן can answer: 'What you take from him comes back onto me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ruling of אביי about who is allowed to argue in court when a creditor takes a field that was sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The creditor is taking the field from שמעון, so you might think only שמעון can argue. But ראובן gave a guarantee, so he will have to pay שמעון back for whatever is taken. Since the loss really lands on ראובן, he counts as a real side in the case.

keyTerms.meaning: A creditor, someone who is owed money
To argue a case in court
An opponent in court, a real party to the case
Comes back

steps.confusionAlert: The creditor is ראובן's creditor, not שמעון's. He takes the field from שמעון only because ראובן owed him money before he sold it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Reuven who sold a field to Shimon with a guarantee,
and Reuven's creditor came
and is seizing it from him (Shimon),
the law is that Reuven may go
and argue the case with him (the creditor),
and the creditor cannot say to him:
You are not my opponent in this case,
because Reuven can say to him: What you take from him
comes back onto me.
phrases.notes: Because of the guarantee, ראובן will have to pay שמעון back, so the loss is really his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רְאוּבֵן שֶׁמָּכַר שָׂדֶה לְשִׁמְעוֹן בְּאַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling about guarantees in sales, connected by topic to the discussion of אחריות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller who gave a guarantee may argue in court against his own creditor who is taking the field from the buyer.

steps.title: Another version: even without a guarantee
steps.stepSummary: A second version of אביי's ruling says ראובן may argue the case even if he sold the field without a guarantee. He can say he does not want שמעון to have a complaint against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: Even if he sold without a guarantee, ראובן may also argue the case, because he can say to the creditor: 'I don't want שמעון to have a complaint against me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of אביי's ruling that goes further than the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, ראובן could argue only because he would lose money. In this version, ראובן loses no money, since there was no guarantee. But he still has a reason to fight: he does not want the buyer to be upset with him for selling a field that got taken away.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (another version of the same statement)
Without a guarantee
A complaint or grievance

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Even if he sold without a guarantee, Reuven may also argue,
because he can say to him: I am not comfortable
with Shimon having a complaint against me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בְּאַחְרָיוּת נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of step 12 that lets ראובן argue even with no guarantee.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a seller who gave no guarantee may argue against the creditor, so the buyer will not have a complaint against him.

steps.title: אביי begins a second case: challengers before possession
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens a new case. ראובן sold a field to שמעון without a guarantee, and people came forward challenging ראובן's ownership before שמעון took possession. The ruling continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: ראובן sold a field to שמעון without a guarantee, and challengers came out against the field. As long as שמעון has not yet taken possession of it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new ruling of אביי. Only the case is given here; the actual ruling comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here people claim the field was never really ראובן's, so the problem is not a creditor. The detail 'before שמעון took possession' is the key point. The coming ruling will turn on whether the buyer has already taken hold of the field.

keyTerms.meaning: Challengers, people who dispute who really owns the field
Took possession of the land

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Do not look for the ruling yet; it comes right after this.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: רְאוּבֵן שֶׁמָּכַר שָׂדֶה לְשִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁלֹּא בְּאַחְרָיוּת,
phrases.english: Reuven who sold a field to Shimon without a guarantee,
